-- An invoice can also take a flat amount off what its line items add up to, on top of (or instead of)
-- the percentage discount. It never takes off more than is left after the percentage. Existing
-- invoices have no flat discount, so their amounts are unchanged.
ALTER TABLE invoice ADD COLUMN discount_amount DECIMAL(12, 2) DEFAULT 0 NOT NULL;

ALTER TABLE invoice ADD CONSTRAINT invoice_discount_amount_non_negative CHECK (discount_amount >= 0);
-- An invoice's discount is now either a percentage or a flat amount, never both. An invoice that had
-- both keeps what they took off together, as a flat amount, so its amount is unchanged: the
-- percentage of the subtotal plus the flat amount (never more than was left after the percentage).
CREATE VIEW invoice_subtotal_v44 AS
    SELECT i.id AS invoice_id,
           COALESCE((SELECT SUM(ROUND(l.qty * l.unit_price, 2)
                         - ROUND(ROUND(l.qty * l.unit_price, 2) * l.discount_pct / 100, 2))
                     FROM invoice_line_item l WHERE l.invoice_id = i.id), 0) AS subtotal
    FROM invoice i;

UPDATE invoice i SET
    discount_amount = (
        SELECT ROUND(v.subtotal * i.discount_pct / 100, 2)
            + LEAST(i.discount_amount, GREATEST(v.subtotal - ROUND(v.subtotal * i.discount_pct / 100, 2), 0))
        FROM invoice_subtotal_v44 v WHERE v.invoice_id = i.id),
    discount_pct = 0
WHERE i.discount_pct > 0 AND i.discount_amount > 0;

DROP VIEW invoice_subtotal_v44;

ALTER TABLE invoice ADD CONSTRAINT invoice_discount_one_kind CHECK (discount_pct = 0 OR discount_amount = 0);
-- An invoice can now carry several discounts at once, each either a percentage or a flat amount off what
-- its line items add up to. Their combined effect comes off before tax: the percentages each take their
-- share of the subtotal, then the flat amounts come off what is left (never more than is left).
CREATE TABLE invoice_discount (
    id              BIGINT GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    invoice_id      BIGINT         NOT NULL,
    discount_pct    DECIMAL(5, 2)  DEFAULT 0 NOT NULL,
    discount_amount DECIMAL(12, 2) DEFAULT 0 NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT invoice_discount_invoice_fk FOREIGN KEY (invoice_id) REFERENCES invoice (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    CONSTRAINT invoice_discount_row_pct_range CHECK (discount_pct >= 0 AND discount_pct <= 100),
    CONSTRAINT invoice_discount_row_amount_non_negative CHECK (discount_amount >= 0),
    CONSTRAINT invoice_discount_row_one_kind CHECK (discount_pct = 0 OR discount_amount = 0),
    CONSTRAINT invoice_discount_row_not_empty CHECK (discount_pct > 0 OR discount_amount > 0)
);

CREATE INDEX invoice_discount_invoice_idx ON invoice_discount (invoice_id);

-- Each invoice's existing discount (only ever one kind) carries over as its single discount, so no
-- amounts change.
INSERT INTO invoice_discount (invoice_id, discount_pct, discount_amount)
SELECT id, discount_pct, discount_amount FROM invoice WHERE discount_pct > 0 OR discount_amount > 0;

ALTER TABLE invoice DROP CONSTRAINT invoice_discount_one_kind;
ALTER TABLE invoice DROP CONSTRAINT invoice_discount_pct_range;
ALTER TABLE invoice DROP CONSTRAINT invoice_discount_amount_non_negative;
ALTER TABLE invoice DROP COLUMN discount_pct;
ALTER TABLE invoice DROP COLUMN discount_amount;
-- An invoice can take a percentage off what its line items add up to. The stored amount remains what
-- is owed, so it is now the subtotal less the discount; existing invoices have no discount.
ALTER TABLE invoice ADD COLUMN discount_pct DECIMAL(5, 2) DEFAULT 0 NOT NULL;

ALTER TABLE invoice ADD CONSTRAINT invoice_discount_pct_range CHECK (discount_pct >= 0 AND discount_pct <= 100);

-- An invoice can also take a flat amount off what its line items add up to, on top of (or instead of)
-- the percentage discount. It never takes off more than is left after the percentage. Existing
-- invoices have no flat discount, so their amounts are unchanged.
ALTER TABLE invoice ADD COLUMN discount_amount DECIMAL(12, 2) DEFAULT 0 NOT NULL;

ALTER TABLE invoice ADD CONSTRAINT invoice_discount_amount_non_negative CHECK (discount_amount >= 0);
-- An invoice's discount is now either a percentage or a flat amount, never both. An invoice that had
-- both keeps what they took off together, as a flat amount, so its amount is unchanged: the
-- percentage of the subtotal plus the flat amount (never more than was left after the percentage).
CREATE VIEW invoice_subtotal_v44 AS
    SELECT i.id AS invoice_id,
           COALESCE((SELECT SUM(ROUND(l.qty * l.unit_price, 2)
                         - ROUND(ROUND(l.qty * l.unit_price, 2) * l.discount_pct / 100, 2))
                     FROM invoice_line_item l WHERE l.invoice_id = i.id), 0) AS subtotal
    FROM invoice i;

UPDATE invoice i SET
    discount_amount = (
        SELECT ROUND(v.subtotal * i.discount_pct / 100, 2)
            + LEAST(i.discount_amount, GREATEST(v.subtotal - ROUND(v.subtotal * i.discount_pct / 100, 2), 0))
        FROM invoice_subtotal_v44 v WHERE v.invoice_id = i.id),
    discount_pct = 0
WHERE i.discount_pct > 0 AND i.discount_amount > 0;

DROP VIEW invoice_subtotal_v44;

ALTER TABLE invoice ADD CONSTRAINT invoice_discount_one_kind CHECK (discount_pct = 0 OR discount_amount = 0);
-- An invoice can now carry several discounts at once, each either a percentage or a flat amount off what
-- its line items add up to. Their combined effect comes off before tax: the percentages each take their
-- share of the subtotal, then the flat amounts come off what is left (never more than is left).
CREATE TABLE invoice_discount (
    id              BIGINT GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    invoice_id      BIGINT         NOT NULL,
    discount_pct    DECIMAL(5, 2)  DEFAULT 0 NOT NULL,
    discount_amount DECIMAL(12, 2) DEFAULT 0 NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT invoice_discount_invoice_fk FOREIGN KEY (invoice_id) REFERENCES invoice (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    CONSTRAINT invoice_discount_row_pct_range CHECK (discount_pct >= 0 AND discount_pct <= 100),
    CONSTRAINT invoice_discount_row_amount_non_negative CHECK (discount_amount >= 0),
    CONSTRAINT invoice_discount_row_one_kind CHECK (discount_pct = 0 OR discount_amount = 0),
    CONSTRAINT invoice_discount_row_not_empty CHECK (discount_pct > 0 OR discount_amount > 0)
);

CREATE INDEX invoice_discount_invoice_idx ON invoice_discount (invoice_id);

-- Each invoice's existing discount (only ever one kind) carries over as its single discount, so no
-- amounts change.
INSERT INTO invoice_discount (invoice_id, discount_pct, discount_amount)
SELECT id, discount_pct, discount_amount FROM invoice WHERE discount_pct > 0 OR discount_amount > 0;

ALTER TABLE invoice DROP CONSTRAINT invoice_discount_one_kind;
ALTER TABLE invoice DROP CONSTRAINT invoice_discount_pct_range;
ALTER TABLE invoice DROP CONSTRAINT invoice_discount_amount_non_negative;
ALTER TABLE invoice DROP COLUMN discount_pct;
ALTER TABLE invoice DROP COLUMN discount_amount;
-- An invoice can take a percentage off what its line items add up to. The stored amount remains what
-- is owed, so it is now the subtotal less the discount; existing invoices have no discount.
ALTER TABLE invoice ADD COLUMN discount_pct DECIMAL(5, 2) DEFAULT 0 NOT NULL;

ALTER TABLE invoice ADD CONSTRAINT invoice_discount_pct_range CHECK (discount_pct >= 0 AND discount_pct <= 100);

# Start the Spring Boot app on $PORT (main class net.officefloor.hq.app.Application). On boot, Flyway
# migrates the empty in-memory H2 up to the current schema; Spring serves the SPA (static/) and the

JAR="$(ls -t target/*.jar 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)"
[ -n "$JAR" ] || { echo "no jar in target/ — run bin/build first" >&2; exit 1; }

echo $! > .run/app.pid

A percentage discount can now have a maximum dollar amount. `bin/e2e` passes: the seeded invoice gets 10% off $1,000, capped at $30, so it shows a $30.00 discount and a $970.00 total.

I also checked the API by hand on a 10% taxed invoice with a $30 cap. The discount came to $30, the tax was worked out on the reduced amount ($97), and the total was $1,067. A request that puts a cap on a flat-amount discount is rejected.

**How it works:** the cap belongs to each discount, not the whole invoice, because invoices can already carry several discounts. When the cap kicks in, the discount takes off the cap amount. That amount is spread across the line items the same way flat discounts already are, so tax on each line stays consistent. A percentage that stays under its cap works exactly as before.

**What changed:**
- **Database:** `V49__discount_cap.sql` adds an optional `discount_cap` column to `invoice_discount`. Existing discounts have no cap, so no amounts change. The database also refuses a cap that is zero or set on a flat discount.
- **Server:**
  - Both the "set discount" and "add discount" requests take an optional `discountCap`. Each discount in the invoice response now includes its cap.
  - The calculation is in `Invoice.java`.
  - The test seed endpoint (`TestSupportController`) accepts `discountCap`, or `cap` on a discount in the list, and works the total out the same way.
- **Front end:**
  - The discount form has an optional "Most it takes off" field, with validation and test id `discount-form-cap`.
  - A capped discount's row reads like "Discount 1 (10%, up to $30.00)", with the cap under test id `discount-row-cap`.
  - No existing test ids were changed.

There are no Java unit tests in the project, so the e2e test and the manual API call are the only checks.
